scenarios.Title: LEO / Lunar Prep CubeSat
scenarios.Objective: Test a mineral-mapping camera in Low Earth Orbit for 6+ months, then safely deorbit.
scenarios.Briefing: Before risking a big lunar mission, NASA wants a cheap pathfinder. Build a CubeSat that tests an imaging camera in Low Earth Orbit and carries enough thrust to deorbit at end of life. Every kilogram and every dollar counts.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: CubeSats are built from 10 cm cubes; a 6U is about the size of a shoebox. NASA's CubeSat Launch Initiative has flown well over a hundred of them. They are cheap, but small: Lunar Flashlight and LunaH-Map, two 6U lunar CubeSats launched in 2022, both missed lunar orbit because of thruster problems. Test first, close to home.

scenarios.Title: LEO Space Weather & Magnetosphere Sentinel
scenarios.Objective: Monitor solar storms and Earth's magnetosphere in Low Earth Orbit for a long 18-month operational life.
scenarios.Briefing: Solar flares and geomagnetic storms threaten astronauts and power grids on Earth. Build a high-reliability Low Earth Orbit sentinel around a Fluxgate Magnetometer & Plasma Boom that survives at least 18 months in orbit. A CubeSat has little room and little power, so every watt counts.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: Space-weather sentinels like NASA's THEMIS and MMS measure magnetic field reconnection and energetic solar wind particles so mission control can warn satellites and astronauts before coronal mass ejections arrive.

scenarios.Title: Lunar South Pole Ice
scenarios.Objective: Map water ice from Low Lunar Polar Orbit for 12+ months.
scenarios.Briefing: Ice in the Moon's permanently shadowed craters could supply Artemis astronauts with water, air and rocket fuel. Put an orbiter in Low Lunar Polar Orbit and map it. Near the pole the Sun skims the horizon (solar at 60%), and every image must squeeze through your radio link.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: In 1998 the neutron spectrometer on NASA's Lunar Prospector found extra hydrogen at the Moon's poles. In 2009 the LCROSS impactor struck Cabeus crater and confirmed water ice in the plume. The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has mapped the poles since 2009. That ice is why Artemis is aiming for the south pole.

scenarios.Title: NASA CAPSTONE Cislunar Pathfinder
scenarios.Objective: Insert a navigation pathfinder into Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) for 6+ months under a tight $65M cap.
scenarios.Briefing: NASA's real 25 kg CAPSTONE spacecraft proved the stability of the Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit planned for the Artemis Gateway station. With a tight $65M budget, build a compact cislunar craft carrying a magnetometer or laser altimeter payload that can reach NRHO and maintain station-keeping for 6 months.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: Launched on an Electron rocket in June 2022, NASA's 12U CAPSTONE CubeSat (25 kg, ~$30M total cost) became the first spacecraft to fly in a Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) around the Moon, testing autonomous cislunar navigation alongside NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

scenarios.Title: NASA LRO Lunar Polar Mapper
scenarios.Objective: Map 3D lunar polar topography and water ice in Low Lunar Polar Orbit for 12+ months (85+ science pts).
scenarios.Briefing: Modeled directly on NASA's 2009 Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO). Enter a 100 km Low Lunar Polar Orbit (800 m/s capture + 10 m/s monthly station-keeping) and combine LOLA 5-beam laser altimetry with spectral/neutron mapping to scout safe Artemis landing zones.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: Launched in June 2009 aboard an Atlas V 401, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (1,916 kg at launch) has mapped the Moon in 3D for over 15 years using the LOLA 5-beam laser altimeter, LROC cameras, and neutron detectors, returning more data than any other planetary mission in history.

scenarios.Title: Far-Side Lander
scenarios.Objective: Land a rover on the lunar far side and relay its data from a halo orbit for 6+ months.
scenarios.Briefing: The far side never faces Earth, so a lander there can't phone home directly. Deliver a rover (about 1100 m/s of descent delta-V) while the carrier parks in a Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit that sees both worlds. Mass, power, data, delta-V and lifetime all bite at once.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: The far side never faces Earth. In January 2019 China's Chang'e 4 made the first soft landing there, talking home through the Queqiao relay satellite beyond the Moon. NASA's CAPSTONE CubeSat (25 kg, launched on an Electron in 2022) tested the near-rectilinear halo orbit planned for the Gateway station.

scenarios.Title: NASA VIPER Polar Ice Drill Mission
scenarios.Objective: Deliver a rover with the TRIDENT Ice Drill & Mass Spectrometer to the lunar south pole (130+ science pts, 45% sunlight).
scenarios.Briefing: Inspired by NASA's VIPER and CLPS PRIME-1 polar surface missions. Descend into the Moon's permanently shadowed south-pole craters (1,150 m/s landing delta-V) where solar arrays only produce 45% power, and drill 1 meter into the regolith to analyze water ice volatiles.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: NASA's VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover) and PRIME-1 missions use the 1-meter TRIDENT rotary-percussive drill and MSolo mass spectrometer to sample subsurface water ice at the lunar south pole, where extreme shadow and cold test power systems to the limit.

scenarios.Title: Deep Cislunar Subsurface & Lava Tube Survey
scenarios.Objective: Conduct a 24-month extended multi-instrument survey of lunar lava tubes and magnetic anomalies (110+ science pts).
scenarios.Briefing: Future lunar habitats will need natural radiation shelter inside ancient volcanic lava tubes. Place a long-endurance orbiter in LLO or NRHO for 24+ months with high-bandwidth downlink and a multi-instrument suite to map surface skylights and crustal anomalies.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: High-resolution laser altimetry and magnetic field mapping have revealed skylights leading into vast underground lunar lava tubes that maintain stable temperatures and shield crews from cosmic radiation and micrometeoroids.

scenarios.Title: Sandbox Mission Lab
scenarios.Objective: Everything unlocked. Build the best-scoring mission you can.
scenarios.Briefing: All parts unlocked and a generous budget. Experiment freely and watch each choice ripple through all six resources.
scenarios.RealMissionBackground: Mission design is a trade study: every choice moves budget, mass, power, data, delta-V and lifetime at once. NASA teams iterate through Concept Maturity Levels until the design closes. In the sandbox everything is unlocked.
